summary: Hand-written regex detectors for surface properties were scored on the four labelled samples; six properties split every sample's labels perfectly and were confirmed as independent in the corpus. Per probe and property, dependence was the ratio of gradient-dotted property direction (corpus mean difference) to gradient-dotted topic direction (sample label difference minus signed property directions, cross-checked with a keyword corpus topic direction); |ratio|>=0.3 marked a cue. Two probes got cues (greeting, hashtag), two none. Latents were picked as the 16 same-sign top contributors to dF_cue*g, compared against cue-fragment and minimal-pair rankings and a curated pool, then checked by sample ablation (separation drop, balanced accuracy) and topic-retention ratios. True logits were spent on long synthetic cue-toggle pairs.

per_probe.procedure: Six label-aligned properties found by detector scan. For probe 0 every property's gradient-dotted corpus direction was small relative to the topic coefficient under both the keyword corpus topic direction and the sample-derived topic direction (all |ratio| well below 0.3). The extended feature scan found no further aligned property. A greeting on/off long pair gave a small proxy shift and a small true-logit shift on this probe.
per_probe.quote: gives a consistent picture: **probe 0 = none, probe 1 = greeting, probe 2 = hashtag, probe 3 = none**

per_probe.conclusion: greeting line at the start of the note
per_probe.procedure: Greeting dependence ratio far above 0.3 (about -1.1 to -1.4) under both topic directions. Regex built from greeting first words seen in corpus and samples, checked on corpus (perfect balanced accuracy, no false positives, no missed greeting lines), scope first_line. Latents: top-16 same-sign by corpus dF_greeting*g; per-token inspection showed several fire on content, so cue-token-focused alternatives (fragments, greeting-with-body deltas) were built, but the alternative set captured less and removed less sample separation under ablation, so the corpus top-16 set was kept. Topic retention and ablated balanced accuracy were checked.

Hashtag dependence ratio about -0.44 to -0.73 depending on topic direction, above 0.3. Regex #\w+ anywhere, verified perfect on corpus. Latents: first the top-16 same-sign by corpus dF_hashtag*g; after token inspection showed some content latents, a pool of hashtag-token latents (from fragments, pairs, examples) was assembled and the top-16 same-sign pool members by corpus contribution were taken. Capture vs corpus, short-pair and long-pair directions, sample ablation (separation drop, balanced accuracy unchanged) and topic retention were checked.
per_probe.quote: Hashtag is token-local, so the all-genuine `final_p2` is optimal.

per_probe.procedure: All six aligned properties had small dependence ratios under the corpus keyword topic direction and the sample-derived one. No further aligned property in the extended scan. A hashtag on/off long pair gave a small proxy shift and a small true-logit change on this probe, consistent with none.

caveats: Greeting and hashtag latent pools and the alternative greeting set were hand-assembled from inspected outputs that are partly truncated in the log, so they are hard-coded constants. Some output tables (probe 2/3 dependence values, part of the context-latent list) were truncated. The pair-consistency selection was computed but never used downstream; it is treated as abandoned. The pool-restricted greeting set was computed but the corpus top-16 set was submitted.
